_comment: Per-title load geometry for tools/decomp_pipeline.py. DATA, not code: adding a title is an
entry here, and the pipeline cross-checks every field against the image's own PS-X EXE header
before it imports anything. A wrong entry is REFUSED, because a wrong base does not fail on
its own -- Ghidra imports happily and every function lands at a plausible address that is not
the one the title's documents name.
field: text_load_address / text_file_offset come from the header's load address and the
fixed 0x800 PS-X EXE text offset. ghidra_base is DERIVED, not stored, so it cannot drift:
it is text_load_address - text_file_offset, which maps file offset 0x800 onto the load
address and leaves the executable's own header below the text window.
field: text_size is optional; when present it is checked too, and it is what bounds the
disassembly window so the tool does not spend its attention on image data.
field: entry is the PS-X EXE entry point, recorded for reference. The pipeline seeds
disassembly from the whole declared window rather than from this one address, because
auto-analysis must reach the jump-table-only handlers that have no call site.
MEASURED 2026-09-28 from the provisioned images in each title repository. Every title in this
workspace is a PS-X EXE loading at 0x80010000 with text at file offset 0x800; they differ in
text size, which is why the size is data here rather than an assumption in the code.

spyro1.note: Insomniac. Its repo verified the file-offset formula against 62,183 of 62,183 recorded instructions.

crash1.note: Naughty Dog. Retail projection is H=1000, OFX=0, OFY=0; widening must not raise the 0x800578D0 GTE near plane.

crashbash.note: Main image has no file extension; find -iname 'SCUS*.BIN' misses it.

ctr.note: Naughty Dog. Measured 2 fields per game frame; 30 fps.

megamanx4.note: Capcom. TRAP: `llvm-objdump --triple=mips` silently misdecodes this image; use plain `llvm-objdump -d`. Its vendored decomp is AGPL-3.0 and may NOT be lifted into psxport or any other workspace repo.

spiderman1.note: Neversoft. Reaches library routines through jalr function pointers, so a jal-only census reads 0 for every one of them.

tekken3.note: Namco. Already 60 fps, so widescreen-only enhancement scope.

tomba1.note: Whoopee Camp. Already 60 fps, so widescreen-only enhancement scope.

tomba2.note: Whoopee Camp. The resident executable is ~15% of the title; most code is in .PRG overlays loaded at run time.

vagrant.note: Square. SHA-1 of this image matches the CC0 rood-reverse decomp's target, so its symbol addresses are confirmed against real bytes -- a reading aid only, never copied into a shipping path. 933,925 B of its code lives in .PRG overlays, which need their own entries and are NOT covered here.
